title: Secondary Student Training Program (SSTP)
summary: A selective 5.5-week summer research program where students work with University of Iowa faculty mentors in their labs, live in a campus residence hall and earn three semester hours of university credit.
eligibility: Students in grades 10-11.
requirements: Online application through the Belin-Blank Center
cost_note: $7,500 program fee covers room, board, materials, activities and 3 semester hours of credit; travel not included
deadline_note: Applications due Feb 16, 2027 at 11:59 pm CST

title: Governor's Scholars Program
summary: A free five-week residential summer program for Kentucky high school juniors, held on three college campuses, built to develop the state's next generation of civic and economic leaders.
eligibility: Kentucky residents in 11th grade at the time of selection who will continue at a Kentucky school the next year and have taken the ACT, PSAT or SAT in grades 9-11.
requirements: Apply through your high school counselor (homeschool students apply directly to the program)
cost_note: Selected scholars attend free of charge
location: Centre College, Morehead State and Murray State, KY
deadline_note: Schools submit applications by Jan 15, 2027 (single-school districts, private schools, homeschool) or Jan 29, 2027 (multi-school districts); your counselor may set an earlier date

title: Governor's Institutes of Vermont Summer Institutes
summary: Residential summer institutes on Vermont college campuses in arts, engineering, entrepreneurship, global issues and youth action, health and medicine, math, technology and design, and weather and climate science.
eligibility: Vermont students in grades 9-11.
requirements: Apply online through GIV
cost_note: Sliding-scale tuition; students can attend for as little as $10
commitment_note: Live on campus for the institute
deadline_note: Applications for 2027 are not open yet; dates not posted on the site

title: Youth Conservation Corps (YCC)
summary: A paid summer job program where teens work on conservation projects in national parks and other federal lands, usually 40 hours a week for 8-10 weeks.
eligibility: Youth ages 15-18 who are permanent U.S. residents and can commute daily to the park (Yellowstone is the only overnight program).
requirements: Apply to a participating park when the season opens
cost_note: At least the state or federal minimum wage, whichever is higher
commitment_note: Generally 8-10 weeks, about 40 hours a week
deadline_note: 2027 applications are expected to open in late January or early February 2027; check the list of participating parks

title: American Computer Science League (ACSL)
summary: A computer science competition taken at school in four contests across the year, with divisions for students of different ages and abilities and no limit on how many students compete.
eligibility: Pre-college students at schools worldwide; a team advisor registers the school and gives students access to the contests.
requirements: Ask a teacher to register your school as an ACSL advisor
cost_note: Registration is by school; fees not stated on the home page
commitment_note: Four contests during the school year
deadline_note: Registration for 2026-27 is open; Contest #1 became available Oct 19, 2026

title: CyberPatriot National Youth Cyber Defense Competition
summary: A team cybersecurity competition where high school and middle school students secure virtual computer systems in online rounds, led by a coach.
eligibility: High school and middle school students on a team registered by an adult coach.
requirements: Join or form a team with a coach
cost_note: $225 per team in the Open Division ($180 if created before July 15); fee waived for the All Service Division
commitment_note: Online rounds during the school year; Round 1 ran Oct 22-25, 2026
deadline_note: Team payment deadline Nov 5, 2026

title: The Earth Prize
summary: A global environmental sustainability competition for students aged 13-19 who propose solutions to environmental problems; seven regional winners each receive USD 10,000.
eligibility: Students aged 13 to 19.
requirements: Register online, then submit your project before submissions close
cost_note: Seven regional winners receive USD 10,000 each ($104,500 in prizes in total)
commitment_note: Phases run from registration through a May 28, 2027 awards ceremony
deadline_note: Registration closes Jan 10, 2027; submissions close Jan 31, 2027

title: Diller Teen Tikkun Olam Awards
summary: Awards of $36,000 each to 15 Jewish teens a year who lead service projects with measurable impact; the money can go toward the recipient's education or initiative.
eligibility: Jewish teens aged 15-19 by the application deadline who live in the U.S. and lead (unpaid) a project run from the U.S.
requirements: Online application describing one project you lead
cost_note: $36,000 per recipient
deadline_note: Nominations due December 2026; applications due January 2027 (exact day not posted)

title: Mississippi Governor's School
summary: A two-week, tuition-free residential honors program at Mississippi University for Women for gifted rising juniors and seniors, sponsored by the State of Mississippi.
eligibility: Mississippi residents currently in 10th or 11th grade who have not attended before and meet the academic and advanced-ability requirements.
requirements: Online application with a résumé and a response to the 2027 scholar prompt; Two recommendation letters (due Nov 1, 2026)
cost_note: Tuition, room, meals and activities covered; scholars pay their own travel and dorm supplies
deadline_note: Final deadline Nov 1, 2026; first-round decisions by Dec 20

title: Iowa Young Writers' Studio Summer Residential Program
summary: Two-week residential creative writing sessions at the University of Iowa, with workshops in fiction, poetry and other forms.
eligibility: Students currently in 10th, 11th or 12th grade; international students may apply.
requirements: Writing sample of up to ten pages; One recommendation letter
cost_note: $2,500 fee for accepted students, plus a $10 reading fee that is waived for those who can't pay
deadline_note: Applications accepted Jan 25 - Feb 7, 2027 (11:59 pm CST); decisions Apr 9, 2027

title: SEO Scholars New York
summary: A free eight-year academic program that takes New York City public high school students to and through college, with Saturday classes, weekday sessions, a summer academy and one-on-one advising in college.
eligibility: Current 9th graders at NYC public high schools with at least a 70% or 2.0 GPA; some charter and specialized schools are not eligible.
requirements: Online application with recent grades; Short writing sample; Teacher recommendation; Income verification
cost_note: Free, including classes, SAT prep and field trips
commitment_note: Three Saturdays a month plus one weekday afternoon a week, and a month each summer after 9th and 10th grade
deadline_note: Applications close Dec 14, 2026; interviews in January

title: SEO Scholars San Francisco
summary: A free eight-year academic program that takes San Francisco students to and through college, with Saturday classes, weekday sessions, a summer academy and one-on-one advising in college.
eligibility: Rising 9th graders in San Francisco; households generally earn no more than $80,000 a year (assessed case by case). About 20-25 spots.
requirements: Online application with recent grades; Income verification (send early)
cost_note: Free, including classes, SAT prep and field trips
commitment_note: Three Saturdays a month plus one weekday afternoon a week, and a month each summer
deadline_note: Deadline Dec 15, 2026; applications are reviewed in the order received

title: Minds Matter
summary: A selective college-prep and mentoring program that starts in 10th grade, pairing students from low-income families with volunteer mentors for writing, test prep and college applications.
eligibility: High-achieving students from low-income families, starting in 10th grade, near one of 14 chapters.
requirements: Apply through your nearest chapter
cost_note: Cost not stated on the program page
commitment_note: Multi-year program from 10th grade through college admission
deadline_note: Each chapter sets its own application dates

title: LEDA Scholars Program
organization: Leadership Enterprise for a Diverse America (LEDA)
summary: A free five-week residential Aspects of Leadership Summer Institute at Princeton and Yale, followed by college guidance and support through college and beyond.
eligibility: Juniors at U.S. public high schools graduating in 2028, U.S. citizens or permanent residents, unweighted GPA 3.5+, household income $90,000 or less.
requirements: Part I online application
cost_note: Summer Institute is free
commitment_note: Five-week residential summer institute, then multi-year college guidance
deadline_note: Part I due Dec 9, 2026

title: Bennington Young Writers Awards
summary: A free writing contest for high school students in fiction, nonfiction or poetry, with cash prizes in each category.
eligibility: Students in grades 9-12 worldwide; 12th graders must first submit a Common or Coalition application and indicate interest.
requirements: One entry of up to 1,500 words (or 1-3 poems)
cost_note: $2,000 first, $1,000 second, $500 third per category; $250 for distinguished entries; no entry fee
deadline_note: Due Nov 1, 2026 at 11:59 pm ET

title: Summer Youth Employment Program (SYEP)
organization: NYC Department of Youth and Community Development
summary: New York City's paid summer jobs program for young people, offering work experience and career exploration.
eligibility: NYC youth ages 14-24.
requirements: Online application when it opens
cost_note: Paid summer work
deadline_note: 2027 dates not posted yet; the 2026 deadline was Mar 13, 2026

title: Step Up Summer Internships
summary: Minneapolis's program placing teens and young adults in paid summer internships, about nine weeks long.
eligibility: Minneapolis residents ages 14-21 who are not enrolled in college.
requirements: Online application when it opens
cost_note: Paid internships
commitment_note: About nine weeks (2026 ran June 22 - Aug 21)
deadline_note: 2027 dates not posted yet; the 2026 window was Jan 5 - Mar 1

title: Grow Detroit's Young Talent (GDYT)
summary: Detroit's summer youth employment program, offering paid summer work to young people across the city.
eligibility: Detroit youth ages 14-24.
requirements: Online application when it opens
cost_note: Paid summer work
deadline_note: 2027 dates not posted yet; the 2026 application ran Mar 13 - May 15, 2026

title: Seattle Youth Employment Program Internships
summary: Paid summer internships for young people through the City of Seattle, running six to eight weeks.
eligibility: Ages 16-24 at the start date who live in Seattle or attend Seattle Public Schools or Seattle Colleges, in households at or below 80% of area median income; proof of work authorization required.
requirements: Online application through Youth Connect
cost_note: $21.30 an hour unless the employer states otherwise
deadline_note: 2027 dates not posted yet; the 2026 internship application ran Mar 18 - May 5

title: Chicago Youth Works
summary: The City of Chicago's youth employment program (formerly One Summer Chicago), offering paid work experience in the summer or year-round.
eligibility: Youth and young adults ages 14-24.
requirements: Create an account and apply online
cost_note: Paid work experience
deadline_note: 2027 application dates not posted on the site

title: West Virginia Governor's Honors Academy
summary: A free three-week residential summer program at West Virginia University for about 175 rising seniors, funded by the State Legislature.
eligibility: West Virginia residents who are juniors when they apply (rising seniors).
requirements: Apply with your school counselor
cost_note: Tuition, room, board and materials paid by the state
deadline_note: 2027 dates not posted yet; the 2026 deadline was Apr 3, 2026

title: High School Summer Research Internship
organization: Price College of Engineering, University of Utah
summary: An eight-week, no-cost summer research internship in University of Utah engineering labs, about 30 hours a week.
eligibility: Rising seniors (graduating in 2028).
requirements: Online registration with a teacher recommendation
cost_note: No cost; interns are not paid; housing not provided
commitment_note: 8 weeks, 30 hours a week, about 9 am - 3 pm weekdays (June 8 - July 31)
deadline_note: Registration is closed for now; the next deadline is not posted

title: Engineering Summer Program (ESP)
summary: A free three-week residential program where students live on campus and take math, physics, chemistry and introductory engineering design taught by UW-Madison faculty.
eligibility: Current sophomores or juniors who are U.S. citizens or permanent residents, have completed a year each of algebra and geometry and have an unweighted GPA of 3.0+.
requirements: Online application
cost_note: Free, including housing and meals
deadline_note: 2027 dates not posted yet; sign up for updates

title: Tennessee Governor's School for the Sciences and Engineering
summary: A four-week on-campus summer program in science and engineering at the University of Tennessee, Knoxville.
eligibility: Rising 11th and 12th graders at Tennessee high schools (current 10th and 11th graders), nominated by high school faculty.
requirements: Apply through the Tennessee Governor's School Unified Application, opened from your high school; student application due Nov 20, 2026, counselor and teacher recommendations due Dec 11, 2026; offers sent Mar 5, 2027.
cost_note: Full scholarships cover all tuition and fees; partial scholarships cover some fees and students pay tuition
deadline_note: Student application due Nov 20, 2026

title: Tennessee Governor's School for the Arts
summary: A three-week summer arts intensive at MTSU in dance, filmmaking, instrumental music, vocal music, theatre and visual art, with students chosen by audition.
eligibility: Tennessee residents in public, private or home schools who are rising 11th or 12th graders.
requirements: Unified application plus an audition in January or February
cost_note: Fees not stated on the program page
deadline_note: Dance, theatre and visual art due Nov 20, 2026; music and filmmaking due Jan 15, 2027

title: Tennessee Governor's School for Computational Physics
summary: A free three-week summer program in computational physics at Austin Peay with daily sessions and field trips, earning four hours of college credit.
eligibility: Rising 11th and 12th graders at Tennessee high schools (current 10th and 11th graders), nominated by high school faculty.
requirements: Apply through the Tennessee Governor's School Unified Application, opened from your high school; student application due Nov 20, 2026, counselor and teacher recommendations due Dec 11, 2026; offers sent Mar 5, 2027.
cost_note: Admission is free with an eligible application
deadline_note: Student application due Nov 20, 2026

title: Tennessee Governor's School for Technological Innovation and Business Leadership
summary: A 28-day residential program at Tennessee Tech covering entrepreneurship, innovation and technology, earning three college credit hours.
eligibility: Rising juniors and seniors at Tennessee public or private high schools who rank near the top of their class or are highly talented in the program's fields.
requirements: Apply through the Tennessee Governor's School Unified Application, opened from your high school; student application due Nov 20, 2026, counselor and teacher recommendations due Dec 11, 2026; offers sent Mar 5, 2027.
cost_note: State funding covers residence halls, tuition, fees and on-campus meals; bring about $100 spending money
deadline_note: Student application due Nov 20, 2026

title: Tennessee Governor's School for the Integration of Biological and Statistical Sciences
summary: A five-week on-campus program at ETSU combining biology and statistics through coursework, speakers and applied projects; students can earn seven college credits.
eligibility: Rising 11th and 12th graders at Tennessee high schools (current 10th and 11th graders), nominated by high school faculty.
requirements: Apply through the Tennessee Governor's School Unified Application, opened from your high school; student application due Nov 20, 2026, counselor and teacher recommendations due Dec 11, 2026; offers sent Mar 5, 2027.; Additional program application linked from the unified application
cost_note: Cost not stated on the program page
deadline_note: Student application due Nov 20, 2026

title: Tennessee Governor's School for the Agricultural Sciences
summary: A four-week summer program at UT Martin giving a broad overview of agriculture and natural resources.
eligibility: Rising 11th and 12th graders at Tennessee high schools (current 10th and 11th graders), nominated by high school faculty.
requirements: Apply through the Tennessee Governor's School Unified Application, opened from your high school; student application due Nov 20, 2026, counselor and teacher recommendations due Dec 11, 2026; offers sent Mar 5, 2027.
cost_note: Cost not stated on the program page
deadline_note: Student and program applications due Nov 20, 2026

title: Live Más Scholarship
summary: A scholarship for young people pursuing their passion, awarded on a short video or essay instead of grades or test scores; recent awards were $25,000.
eligibility: Ages 16-26, legal residents of the 50 states or D.C. (or dependents of active-duty U.S. military), planning to enroll or enrolled in a two-year, four-year, vocational or trade program.
requirements: Video (30 seconds - 2 minutes) or essay (250-500 words) about your passion
cost_note: Awards of up to $25,000; renewable up to three times
deadline_note: Application window Oct 13, 2026 - Jan 5, 2027 at 5 pm PST

title: Apprenticeships in STEAM Exploration (ASE)
summary: Competitive four- to eight-week summer STEM internships designed by mentors at universities, hospitals, research institutes and companies in the Portland and Corvallis areas.
eligibility: Rising 10th, 11th and 12th graders who live within 50 miles of the internship (some positions list a minimum age).
requirements: Online application choosing positions from the internship catalog
cost_note: Cost or pay not stated on the program page
deadline_note: The 2027 application opens in January 2027; the 2026 deadline was Mar 6, 2026

title: Stanford AIMI Summer Health AI Bootcamp
organization: Stanford Center for Artificial Intelligence in Medicine and Imaging (AIMI)
summary: A two-week virtual bootcamp introducing machine learning and its uses in health care, designed for high school students of all technical backgrounds.
eligibility: High school students; no technical background required.
requirements: Online application
cost_note: Cost not stated on the program page
deadline_note: Applications open Nov 10, 2026 and close Feb 1, 2027

title: Stanford AIMI Summer Research Internship
organization: Stanford Center for Artificial Intelligence in Medicine and Imaging (AIMI)
summary: A two-week virtual research internship where high school students work with real-world health data on mentored projects in AI and medicine.
eligibility: High school students.
requirements: Online application
cost_note: Cost not stated on the program page
deadline_note: Applications open Nov 10, 2026 and close Feb 1, 2027

title: KEYS Research Internship
summary: A summer research internship in University of Arizona labs for Arizona high school students, ending in a research showcase; no cost and three units of credit.
eligibility: Students 16 or older by June 7, 2027 who are in high school, U.S. citizens or permanent residents, and Arizona residents for at least a year.
requirements: Online application with four essays; Two recommenders (one a science teacher); Unofficial transcript; Signed student and parent agreement
cost_note: No cost to participate; 3 units of MCB credit
deadline_note: Application opens Nov 2, 2026; recommendations must be in by Jan 7, 2027

title: Thrive Scholars
summary: A free six-year program from 11th grade into a career, with 200+ hours of summer calculus and writing instruction, college admissions and financial aid guidance, and mentoring.
eligibility: High school juniors in the U.S. with an unweighted GPA of 3.60+ and household income of $125,000 or less.
requirements: Online application; Transcript and 11th-grade report card; Household tax return; Recommendations (due Jan 18)
cost_note: The program is free
commitment_note: Six years, from 11th grade through college
deadline_note: Applications due Dec 20, 2026 at 11:59 pm PT; decisions mid-March

title: Hispanic Heritage Foundation Youth Awards
summary: Recognizes high school seniors in categories such as STEM, entrepreneurship, media and public service; Gold, Silver and Bronze recipients get a one-time grant for college or a community service effort.
eligibility: High school seniors graduating in spring 2027 with an unweighted GPA of 3.0+ who will enroll in college in 2027-28.
requirements: Online application; Attend a virtual regional ceremony if selected
cost_note: One-time grant for Gold, Silver and Bronze recipients
deadline_note: Deadline Nov 1, 2026

title: SEES Summer High School Intern Program
organization: NASA and the Center for Space Research, UT Austin
summary: NASA's STEM Enhancement in Earth Science internship: virtual learning in the spring and early summer, then two weeks on site at UT Austin working on Earth and space science projects.
eligibility: For 2026: current sophomores or juniors who are U.S. citizens, 16 by the program start, and not past SEES interns.
requirements: Online application
cost_note: Cost not stated on the eligibility page
commitment_note: Virtual May-July, then about two weeks on site in Austin
deadline_note: 2027 dates not posted yet; the 2026 deadline was Feb 22, 2026

title: QuestBridge College Prep Scholars Program
summary: A program for high-achieving juniors from lower-income families with summer program scholarships, college admissions conferences, free college visits and application guidance.
eligibility: High school juniors earning mostly A's in the hardest courses offered, from households earning under $65,000 a year (family of four) with minimal assets.
requirements: Online application
cost_note: Summer program scholarships and free college visits for selected scholars
commitment_note: Junior year into the senior-year National College Match
deadline_note: 2027 dates not posted yet

title: HOBY State Leadership Seminars
summary: Three- to four-day leadership seminars for high school sophomores held in states across the country each spring and summer, with workshops on leadership strengths and values.
eligibility: High school sophomores nominated by their school or community.
requirements: School or community nomination
cost_note: Fees not stated on the seminar page
location: Seminars in states across the U.S.
commitment_note: 3-4 days; most 2027 seminars late May - late June
deadline_note: School nominations are open; no deadline posted

title: Naval Academy Summer Seminar
summary: A six-day summer session at the U.S. Naval Academy giving high school juniors a look at academy academics, leadership and life as a midshipman.
eligibility: Current high school juniors.
requirements: Online application
cost_note: $575 covers lodging, meals and clothing
deadline_note: Applications open Jan 5, 2027 and close Mar 31, 2027 (some parts of the page still say TBD)

title: Academy Introduction Mission (AIM)
summary: A one-week summer program at the Coast Guard Academy for students entering their senior year, with in-person sessions and a free virtual session.
eligibility: Students entering their senior year of high school (apply during junior year).
requirements: Online application
cost_note: $750 tuition for in-person sessions; the virtual session is free; travel not included
commitment_note: Six-day in-person sessions or a two-day virtual session
deadline_note: Applications open in early February and are due April 1
